svg.title: SWE-599 system overview
svg.desc: The v1 benchmark was audited (nine problems) and rebuilt as a leak-free v2 pipeline running only local models. Embedding models lead on citation labels; listwise Llama 3.2 3B follows candidate order and ranks last, and Llama 3.1 8B is better but favours late candidates. Phase 5 ranks each query against an 11,967-work corpus with a leakage-controlled co-citation graph, which adds nothing significant. On human expertise labels (Stelmakh et al.) Qwen3-Embedding again has the lowest loss and no LLM method or fusion beats it. The deployed app has dropped its LLM stage.
svg.text: SWE-599: audit of v1, a leak-free v2 benchmark, graph expansion, and human-label validation
Does reranking with a small local LLM help scientific paper recommendation? On citation and on human expertise labels: no.
Audit: 9 problems (F1–F9) → the v1 headline was an artifact
positives shown first · prompt example hinted a positive · fallback to input order
negatives lacked concepts · positives carried other papers' text (index bug)
nDCG mis-normalized · salted hash() seeds · SPECTER2 wrong pooling
4 · Phase 5 (Oct 2026): full corpus, leakage-controlled graph, reranking (notebooks 07–12)
Positives reachable through the graph: 54.7% (62.9% with raw dates)
Leaks caught: a 2012 copy with 10/10 refs; 24% year-only dates
5 · human expertise labels: Stelmakh et al. gold standard (notebooks 14–18)
Llama 3B listwise, best first / worst first

g.text: Next: a calibrated cut-off, ingest fixes, feedback export

svg.text: evidence: no LLM reranker beats the embedding on either label source
